newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rheinhyp says plans 1.5-2 bln Eurofranc issue.
newsitem.headline: Rheinhyp says plans 1.5-2 bln Eurofranc issue.

text.p: Rheinische Hypothekenbank (Rheinhyp) is planning a Eurofranc issue of between 1.5 billion and two billion francs, Georges Ruchti, Rheinhyp assistant vice president told a news conference on Friday.

Rheinhyp officials, who held a roadshow for French investors on Friday morning, said they had not yet decided what maturity the bond would have and said there was a possibility they would leave some of the proceeds in francs.
"It will be a large issue ... a total of between 1.5 and two billion," Ruchti said. "We haven't thought about the maturity yet."
Oliver Berger at Rheinhyp said the six- and 12-year areas of the French curve looked attractive at the moment.
Rheinhyp officials declined to comment specifically on what yield spread over French government bonds (OATs) they hoped to sell their bonds.

Nine-and-a-half-year Rheinhyp mortgage-backed Pfandbriefe were trading at 15 basis points above German government bonds earlier on Friday, while its five-year Pfandbriefe was trading 12 basis points above government bonds.
Its mortgage bonds, however, carry a triple-A rating, better than the Aa2 Moody's rating for Rheinhyp unsecured senior debt.
"The spread will be higher because it's not the same rating," said Ruchti.
The issue will come from Rheinhyp Finance NV, the German bank's Dutch financing vehicle with an explicit and unconditional guarantee from Rheinhyp.
